new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File checked: (27 pp., text for pp.171-185; wordlist pp.186-197 image-only) and its. At p.185, 'Appendix Two: Wordlists', the introductory note reads exactly as quoted (the compiler '[..]' elides the sentences on why phonetic rather than phonemic transcription was chosen; only typographic quote marks differ): '..An asterisk indicates information which I believe to be incorrect after having confirmed lists with other speakers in the same area. Phonetic stress is word-final unless otherwise indicated. Statistics for lexical similarity were generated using.. WORDSURV'. Identity: I rendered p.186 and read the table header: columns are Farsi-Shirazi formal, Farsi-Bushehri, 'S Luri-Mamasani 1', '…
new_statements.rule_in_words: In Anonby's field transcriptions of Luri varieties (including the four Southern Luri wordlists), phonetic stress falls on the last syllable of the (citation-form) word by default; deviations are marked individually. MacKinnon's Iranica survey adds, for Lori dialects generally, that enclitic ezafe/indefinite/relative/object markers are unstressed, past/perfect stems are stressed on their final syllable, present-tense personal endings are stressed, and negative na-/ma- and subjunctive/imperative ba- attract stress.
new_statements.exceptions: 'unless otherwise indicated' (individual items marked in the image-only wordlists, not legible via scanned). From MacKinnon (pan-Lori): unstressed enclitics (-e ezafe, -i indefinite/relative, -ne/-na object marker), stressed verbal prefixes na-/ma-/ba- with stress shifting off the ending under negation/subjunctive; past-tense personal suffixes unstressed.
new_statements.domain_note: Citation forms in an elicited 225-item wordlist (isolated words), transcribed phonetically; a transcription default rather than an analysed phonological rule. The author's monograph (Anonby 2003a, LINCOM) has a dedicated stress/intonation section that would supersede this.
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted statement (Anonby 2003 JRAS p.185) is a transcription note covering all of Anonby's Luri wordlists; the Southern Luri lists in it are Mamasani 1, Mamasani 2 (Fars), Boyerahmadi and Kohgiluyeh (Kohgiluyeh va Boyer Ahmad) -- all sout2647. Anonby's fuller LINCOM monograph (2003a, not obtained) describes Mamasani Southern Lori of Fars Province specifically (per Taheri-Ardali et al. 2026: 77-78). MacKinnon's Iranica statements are pan-Lori (Northern Lori nort2645, Bakhtiari bakh1245 and Southern Lori together); Windfuhr's Iranica sketch is Boirahmadi (sout2647). Glottolog files Emadi's Marvdashti (Fars) work under sout2647 but its affiliation (Southern Luri vs a Fars Persian dialect) was not verifiable here.

SLori Mamasani/Boir Ahmadi): ezafe -e, relative -i, indefinite -i and definite-object -ne/-na are unstressed; NLori plural suffixes stressed; 'The final syllable of the past and perfect stems is stressed. Presents are stressed on the personal ending except when negated or in the subjunctive mood, in which case stress shifts to the prefix.'; negative na-/ma- and subjunctive/imperative ba- stressed; past-tense personal suffixes unstressed.
